text:
ConocoPhillips jumped 3.4% today to $146.51, extending a sharp two-week rally that's seen the stock climb 15.6%. The driver is oil prices: U.S. crude sits at $101.91 a barrel while global crude has surged to $126.55, a massive gap. That spread widened because of geopolitical supply disruptions—Iran's escalating attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz pushed Brent oil to $110 earlier this week, and tanker rates have spiked so high that the *actual* cost to physically deliver oil is running about $38 per barrel above the headline price. As a major oil producer, ConocoPhillips benefits directly when the price of crude rises and global energy costs spike.

That said, the recent news about sanctions relief on Russian crude (announced 2026-10-19) ordinarily would have pressured oil prices by raising hopes of more supply hitting the market. But the Iran risk and tight physical supply appear to be overwhelming that effect for now, keeping prices elevated and the stock's momentum intact.
